## Summary

Samsung Electro-Mechanics was established in 1973 as Samsung Sanyo Parts, is headquartered in Suwon, South Korea, and is a Samsung Group subsidiary in which Samsung Electronics holds 23.69 percent [2]. It makes MLCCs, inductors and resistors, IC and semiconductor substrates, camera modules, network modules and printed circuit boards [2]. The IEEE registry lists 18 MA-L blocks under this exact spelling; SAMSUNG ELECTRO-MECHANICS(THAILAND) holds 34 more under its own name and is not an alias here [1].

A MAC in these blocks is most likely a network module made by Samsung Electro-Mechanics inside a Samsung or third-party product, so the device brand is usually not the registrant [2][3]. DeviWiki documents the SWL-2210M, a Mini PCI 802.11b module silkscreened SAMSUNG ELECTRO-MECHANICS and built on Intersil PRISM 2.5 (ISL3874 and ISL3685), and the SWL-2210P PCI adapter that carries it under FCC ID E2XSWL-2210P [3][4].

SOLUM was spun off from Samsung Electro-Mechanics in 2015 [5]. No CVE naming the company was found in NVD [6]. The company's site returned errors and the FCC ID databases refused automated access, so the E2X grantee name and any newer modules are not confirmed, and randomization is unknown.
